mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at the decision point signals an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS (level) and 5-day SPX returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.3% in the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings weakness, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) has a negative Rank IC with 20-day SPX returns over any 3-year rolling window, or the joint signal produces negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending economic deceleration that leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month are followed by positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level above 2000 thousand units signals strong residential construction activity that precedes economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 2000.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) at the decision point indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between PAYEMS (level) and 5-day SPX returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) signals active monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction term (CPIAUCSL * FEDFUNDS) has a positive Rank IC with 20-day SPX returns over any 3-year rolling window, or the joint signal produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases.
